searchText: Checking! I think preliminary results with exex is good, but we don't want to use this to base our final results off of because its pretty reth specific For the rewind penalty, I would expect clients to have implemented some sort of cache/storage for this -- ie whenever a block is validated, they would also generate the Execution Witness in place and save it somewhere -- this is probably not too bad to implement I think <@944007601400741989> ? Which part is reth specific? You mean the database lookup latency? We already have this implemented in the reth witness indexer Does enginePayloadWithWitness serialize twice? ie once for engine API to send to the CL and then another to get it from the CL? Yeah... I think this would be important to have. Though the draw down was not much (in latency), but some client could support rewind of block depth > 64 Ah I meant exex as concept -- my thinking is that these optimizations would be in the clients (unless they are too invasive, but not sure that has been the case) They probably only need to support rewinding upto N blocks where N is how deep of a reorg they can do? Agreed I think it should be inside the core client. In that case, it would be more performant. I think we should add custom pruning functionality as is done with most other archived storage items. That's how we've done it in the reth witness indexer. You mean like allow someone to specify whether they want to keep only the first 10 witnesses? Yeah... that's what it seems (in RETH and ETHREX). Geth errors and becomes stall exactly, or maybe it could be based on some rpc invocation to prune all witnesses below block x etc. But clients will probably configure based on their user requirements. Makes sense! I'm trying to get an understanding of the results from first principles. With the engine_newPayload + debug_executionWitness route: - The client would need to execute the block twice - The second execution currently also involves rewinding (but should be minor if we call debug_executionWitness immediately after) - This also involves two serialization roundtrips for each call Does that sound correct? yes... all correct Do you know where I can find a description of engine_newPayloadWithWitness? Which client? Ah mainly just a general description I still named it `engine_newPayloadV3` and `engine_newPayloadV4` just change the internal logic Is it just an EL endpoint that remove the serialization overhead of debug_executionWitness ? I think the key takeaway, in my opinion, is that JSON-RPC is a no-go. I think it's still possible that `engine_newPayloadWithWitness` could be fine if we had more efficient transport. Yeah, and also re-execution as the witness is sent immediately execution is done... (most client have an efficient way for doing this) > JSON-RPC is a no-go. Yeah agree 😄 How would the prover get the witness with engine_newPayloadWithWitness? It would have to be sent in the request_proofs payload body My understanding is that thats a method the CL calls on the EL, so is the idea here that the prover calls engine_newPayloadWithWitness as opposed to the CL? I think the CL would call engine_newPayloadWithWitness when doing payload validation and then include the witness in the request_proofs call to the proof node? from the CL, I think... we kinda talk on this based on the propose design from our early discussion [here](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1463293742457815329/1463297528052191315/image.png?ex=69a2c1c5&is=69a17045&hm=3adf31b237c0ddc3bfb59a5ed4cb315fece6fddc50b95bc0d2a8c1c3b45816fa&_) Ah with this, I think newPayload + debug_executionWitness would have never been reasonable? newPayload + debug_executionWitness would have only been okay if the prover was the one calling debug_executionWitness I think yeah The previous design had the prover call debug_executionWitness which is one reason why EWS is a bit annoying to setup since we need to listen for new blocks from the CL and then get the witness from the EL <@402080271563751435> I'm wondering how we will convince folks to change the engine api from json rpc 😄 In some sense, they already have If I'm not mistaken engine api already supports IPC and web socket We would not be proposing deprecation of pre-existing solutions just support for a new more efficient transport mode Maybe we also use a different namespace zk_newPayloadWithWitness? (I'm not familiar with the engine api dos and donts) I don't think this is the case right now... Ahh it only supports json-rpc? yeah... IPC support was enabled only for the normal external RPC calls (e.g the "eth_" namesapce)

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Checking! I think preliminary results with exex is good, but we don't want to use this to base our final results off of because its pretty reth specific

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: For the rewind penalty, I would expect clients to have implemented some sort of cache/storage for this -- ie whenever a block is validated, they would also generate the Execution Witness in place and save it somewhere -- this is probably not too bad to implement I think <@944007601400741989> ?

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: Which part is reth specific? You mean the database lookup latency?

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: We already have this implemented in the reth witness indexer

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Does enginePayloadWithWitness serialize twice? ie once for engine API to send to the CL and then another to get it from the CL?

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: Yeah... I think this would be important to have. Though the draw down was not much (in latency), but some client could support rewind of block depth > 64

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Ah I meant exex as concept -- my thinking is that these optimizations would be in the clients (unless they are too invasive, but not sure that has been the case)

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: They probably only need to support rewinding upto N blocks where N is how deep of a reorg they can do?

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: Agreed I think it should be inside the core client. In that case, it would be more performant.

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: I think we should add custom pruning functionality as is done with most other archived storage items. That's how we've done it in the reth witness indexer.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: You mean like allow someone to specify whether they want to keep only the first 10 witnesses?

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: Yeah... that's what it seems (in RETH and ETHREX). Geth errors and becomes stall

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: exactly, or maybe it could be based on some rpc invocation to prune all witnesses below block x etc.

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: But clients will probably configure based on their user requirements.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Makes sense!

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
I'm trying to get an understanding of the results from first principles.

With the engine_newPayload + debug_executionWitness route:

- The client would need to execute the block twice
- The second execution currently also involves rewinding (but should be minor if we call debug_executionWitness immediately after)
- This also involves two serialization roundtrips for each call

Does that sound correct?

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: yes... all correct

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Do you know where I can find a description of engine_newPayloadWithWitness?

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: Which client?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Ah mainly just a general description

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: I still named it `engine_newPayloadV3` and `engine_newPayloadV4` just change the internal logic

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Is it just an EL endpoint that remove the serialization overhead of debug_executionWitness ?

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: I think the key takeaway, in my opinion, is that JSON-RPC is a no-go. I think it's still possible that `engine_newPayloadWithWitness` could be fine if we had more efficient transport.

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: Yeah, and also re-execution as the witness is sent immediately execution is done... (most client have an efficient way for doing this)

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
> JSON-RPC is a no-go.
Yeah agree 😄

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: How would the prover get the witness with engine_newPayloadWithWitness?

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: It would have to be sent in the request_proofs payload body

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: My understanding is that thats a method the CL calls on the EL, so is the idea here that the prover calls engine_newPayloadWithWitness as opposed to the CL?

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: I think the CL would call engine_newPayloadWithWitness when doing payload validation and then include the witness in the request_proofs call to the proof node?

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: from the CL, I think... we kinda talk on this based on the propose design from our early discussion [here](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1463293742457815329/1463297528052191315/image.png?ex=69a2c1c5&is=69a17045&hm=3adf31b237c0ddc3bfb59a5ed4cb315fece6fddc50b95bc0d2a8c1c3b45816fa&_)

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
Ah with this, I think newPayload + debug_executionWitness would have never been reasonable?

newPayload + debug_executionWitness would have only been okay if the prover was the one calling debug_executionWitness I think

excerpts.author: developeruche
excerpts.content: yeah

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: The previous design had the prover call debug_executionWitness which is one reason why EWS is a bit annoying to setup since we need to listen for new blocks from the CL and then get the witness from the EL
